name: Cross-sectional coin ranking (point-in-time)
activity: closed - paper book kept as a yardstick
activity_note: Closed by the operator on 2026-10-21: every improvement failed walk-forward and the plain BTC-gated basket matched it. Code and runs in research/plan_v2 (ARCHIVED.md). Successor: System 12.
hypothesis: A model trained only on the past can rank the most-traded coins well enough that holding the top few beats holding them all, out of sample and after honest costs.
data: point-in-time top-14 lists by turnover, delisted coins included, 2018-2026
mechanism: MLP rankers per (timeframe, horizon); for year N the 10 best of 36 configurations on earlier years are averaged; BTC > MA100 gate; exposure scaled to an 18% drawdown budget; fills at the next bar.

helped.effect: removed the biases that inflated Systems 06-10 (+25%/+59% became -9%/-15%)
nested Sharpe +0.64, positive on 100 of 100 seed pairs

helped.what: Selection by 'positive every past year, better toward today'
Exposure scaled to the drawdown budget

hurt.what: Price exits (stop, trailing, take profit, time)
hurt.effect: no gain walk-forward; trailing stop halves the return
walk-forward pick no better than the median idea
none beat it; the plain BTC-gated basket matched it at equal risk

open.what: A coin ranking inside System 12's regime
open.why: System 11 never beat the gated basket; untested inside a better regime

rules: Compare any model with the plain basket under the same gate, at equal risk
Judge a search by the year after the choice, never by its best result
Small positions turn good-looking trades into a small book return
Size pays only in bull years
2026 is read, never used to choose
